subject: A few things I noticed about Papini's online presence
body:
Hi Richard,

You've worked on my 2015 Mustang, so I know the quality that comes out of your shop firsthand. I run a small studio that helps shops like yours capture more work online, and I spent some time looking at how Papini's shows up on the web. I put together a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- Strong, specialized reputation — the reviews you do have call out your communication and honesty, which is exactly what people want from a performance shop
- Clear breakdown of services on the site (Trans-Am, LSX, dyno tuning, suspension)

Where you're leaving money on the table
- No after-hours capture. The shop is Mon–Fri 9–5, so anyone who finds you on a Saturday — when enthusiasts are actually thinking about builds — hits a phone nobody answers. A missed oil change is small; a missed engine build or tune is thousands walking to the next shop.
- No way to book or request a quote online. It's call-or-nothing. A lot of younger customers won't pick up the phone — they'll fill out a form or move on.
- Your reputation is invisible on your own site. You've got happy customers on Yelp and elsewhere, but none of that shows up on papinisgarage.com — so someone deciding between you and another shop never sees it.
- The site is hard to find on Google. It's missing the basic behind-the-scenes setup (business info, hours, location markup) that tells Google to surface you for "performance shop near me" searches.

None of this is urgent, and your work speaks for itself — but each of these is quietly costing you jobs that are already trying to reach you.

If you ever want, I'm happy to walk through how a couple of these could be fixed cheaply. Either way, figured the audit might be useful to you.

Best,
Leo Lebel
cheddar.lebel@gmail.com
